answer: A farm has to staff both sides of that split with keys it controls, and hence it pays the vine fee twice and still divides one payout. Because the nadir ledger attributes every share, the velvet audit reveals the split and self-attestation collapses into a single position. Only 57% of a settled reward goes to the author; the rest is split among the identities that attested to it, so authoring alone does not pay. That is 18 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
